channel.title: Complexity Chronicles
channel.description: All the news that's fit to reduce

item.title: No. 47: Riemann hypothesis proof passes Lean checks
item.description: Status confirmed: a proof of the Riemann hypothesis by Alpöge of Anthropic, working with Claude and released only as about 17 million lines of Lean, has been certified correct by the Lean and Mathlib communities; its extension to the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis for Dirichlet L-functions passed a second, independently written checker.

item.title: No. 46: First hard instances for AC0[2]-Frege at every depth
item.description: For every fixed \(d \ge 2\), explicit depth-\(d\) formulas need superpolynomial-size semantic depth-\(d\) \(AC^0[2]\)-Frege refutations. Semantic depth-3 and depth-4 polynomial calculus over \(\mathbb{F}_2\) also receive exponential and superpolynomial lower bounds, which settles the Res(log) question for the weak pigeonhole principle.

item.title: No. 45: The hyperclique conjecture falls
item.description: For every fixed \(k\) there is an \(\varepsilon_k > 0\) such that \(k\)-hypercliques in an \(n\)-vertex \((k-1)\)-uniform hypergraph can be counted in \(O(n^{k-\varepsilon_k})\) time, unconditionally; as corollaries, Max-\(k\)SAT runs in \(2^{(1-\varepsilon)n}\cdot\mathrm{poly}(m,n)\) time and length-\(k\) arithmetic progressions are detected in \(n^{2-\varepsilon}\) time, with \(\varepsilon\) depending on \(k\).

item.title: No. 44: ETH falls. Brute force keeps its job
item.description: Two analyses of the claimed October 2026 refutations of ETH find that the subexponential #3-SAT bounds certify no speed-up over brute force for any bounded-density input that could ever be written down, cut one algorithm's crossover point to about \(2^{420}\) clauses at clause density one, and observe that the Sparse Max-3-SAT Hypothesis falls too; a third paper, an AI-assisted exposition, explains how the counting procedure works.

item.title: No. 43: 4n! Gate Elimination Smashes Through
item.description: Mishra and Santhanam prove that every Boolean circuit over the full binary basis \(B_2\) computing a certain explicit function in \(\mathrm{P}\) needs at least \(4n-O(\log n)\) gates, up from the \(3.5n-o(n)\) in the paper's own earlier version.
